S79.01.note: The picker trigger label was not found in the files checked; Auto row selection code is in apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx.
steps: Sign in on a paid plan and open the model picker from the chat composer.
Choose the row labelled Auto.
Send a short question, then a harder coding question in a new chat.
Compare the answers: Auto should pick a model for each message and a "Moved to" line appears when it changes model.

S79.02.needs: a paid account (free plans see fewer models)
S79.02.note: Individual model row labels were not read from the file; the picker trigger label was not found.
steps: Open the model picker from the chat composer.
Choose a specific model from the list (for example under Recommended).
Send a message.
Check the answer is from the chosen model: no "Moved to" line should appear.
S79.02.where: Composer model picker > choose a named model row

S79.03.note: Sidebar path "Projects" and the save button text were not verified in the files read.
steps: Open a project from the sidebar.
Open Project settings.
Under Default model, pick a model from the dropdown and save.
Start a new chat inside that project and check the model shown in the composer is the default.
S79.03.where: Projects > open a project > Project settings > Default model

S79.04.note: Task-specific behaviour is in the profile rows; the description says the most capable model, not specifically premium for coding.
steps: Open the model picker from the chat composer.
Choose the row labelled Best under the Auto section.
Send a harder coding or reasoning question.
Check the answer and the model note; it should come from the most capable model your plan includes.
Open the model picker from the chat composer.
Choose the row labelled Instant.
Send a simple question.
Check the answer comes back quickly and the model is one of your plan's fastest models.
Open the model picker from the chat composer.
Choose the row labelled Best.
Send a hard question.
Check the answer model is the most capable one your plan includes.
Open the model picker from the chat composer.
Choose the row labelled Economy.
Send a simple task.
Check the answer model is a low-cost one that can handle the task.

S79.08.note: There is no single privacy-first profile; privacy is set as a workspace policy. Sidebar path to Workspace policy was not verified.
steps: Open the Workspace policy page (admin only).
Under Allowed privacy modes and Default privacy mode, read the Local option.
Set Default privacy mode to Local and save.
Check that Local shows the hint "On-device models. Nothing leaves the machine."

S79.09.note: Intent classification is server-side inner behaviour; its effect shows only through model changes.
steps: Send a coding question and then a plain chat question in the same chat.
Compare which model label appears under each answer ("Moved to" line if the model changed).

S79.10.note: Tool classification is server-side (request-processor); no direct control found.
steps: Ask for something that needs a web search, then a question that does not.
Compare which model answers, using the "Moved to" line if shown.

S79.11.note: The routing to a multimodal model happens automatically in some cases; the button shows only when a conflict exists.
steps: Attach an image in the chat composer while the current model cannot read images.
Look for the message "No model on your plan can read this attachment." or click Choose a compatible model.
Pick a model from the list.
Check the attachment is sent and the answer reads the image.
S79.11.where: Chat composer > attach an image > Choose a compatible model

S79.12.note: Complexity classification is internal; no visible setting found.
steps: Send a short simple question and then a long multi-step question.
Compare the model and depth of the answers.

S79.13.note: Freshness detection is server-side (request-processor); I did not verify the exact visible result.
steps: Ask about a current event such as today's news.
Check whether the answer uses fresh sources.

S79.14.needs: a Free account and a paid account
S79.14.note: Filtering is applied before ranking; the effect is seen as a different model list per plan.
steps: Open the model picker on a Free account and on a paid account.
Compare which models are listed.

S79.15.note: Provider-route choice has no visible control; it is server-side ranking.
steps: Send a message on a chosen model and check the answer comes back without an error.

S79.16.note: The lock is behaviour; visible proof is the absence of the "Moved to" line.
steps: Pick a specific model in the model picker.
Send several messages.
Check no answer shows a "Moved to" line, so the model is never swapped.

S79.19.note: Quota-aware selection is in request-processor; the exact limit message was not verified.
steps: Use a Free account until its usage limit is near.
Send messages and check the model still answers or a limit message shows.

S79.20.note: Fallback notice text was not read; the failure cannot be forced from the UI.
steps: If a model call fails, look under the answer for a fallback notice (role status, data-testid fallback-reason-notice).
Check an answer still arrives.

S79.21.note: Only the attachment conflict switch (Choose a compatible model, ChatComposerNew.tsx) was found; no general better-model one-click offer was found in the code read.

S79.24.note: The catalogue route is apps/web/app/models/compare/page.tsx; the sidebar path and the second answer-comparison button label were not verified.
steps: Open the models catalogue page.
Tick at least two models using their compare checkboxes.
Click the Compare button.
Check the comparison table lists the chosen models side by side.

S79.26.note: The line appears only when a move happened.
steps: Use Auto in a chat and send a message that makes Auto change model.
Look under the answer for the line starting "Moved to" with the model name and reason.
Check the reason explains why Auto chose or moved to that model.
S79.26.where: Chat answer > line under the answer that starts "Moved to"

S79.27.note: The receipt line under an answer (MessageBubble.tsx) appears only when a model escalation happened; a general model label on every answer was not found.

S79.28.note: Policy versioning is server-side (routing-trace.ts, routing-decision-trace-service.ts); no visible control found.

S79.30.note: Fallback to a safe default is server-side (task-family.ts); visible effect is a normal answer.
steps: Send a short ambiguous message such as "hi" with Auto selected.
Check an answer still arrives from a default model.
